name: Companion
description: A coding agent that stays with you in the app: its cursor follows what you write, and it answers in bubbles, comments on lines (threads in the sidebar), suggests changes you take with Tab, or writes with you. Write @claude in a note to ask it something, or @ and a new name to start another. One always-on session of Claude Code or Codex, in a terminal on this machine.

mode.label: Mode
mode.description: how much it does: off; quiet, it answers only what you ask it (@claude in a note, Ask companion); notice, it also sees what you write when you pause and comments when it's useful; pair, it may also write in your notes

agent.label: Agent
agent.description: the coding agent its session runs (claude, codex, claude_personal...)

name.label: Name
name.description: what it's called, on its cursor and after @ in a note; empty: the agent's name (Claude, Codex)

model.label: Model
model.description: the model a new session runs (sonnet, opus, haiku, a full name), for an agent that takes one (Claude Code; others run their own). A quicker one answers sooner

effort.label: Effort
effort.description: how hard its model thinks (low, medium, high, xhigh, max), for an agent that takes it (Claude Code). Less answers sooner

comments.label: Comments
comments.description: where its comments and suggestions show: in the Conversations panel (a dot by each one's line), or as cards beside the text

pause.label: Pause before it looks
pause.description: seconds without typing before it sees what you wrote (Notice and Pair); more mid-sentence

fresh_after.label: Fresh session after
fresh_after.description: moments it handles before a fresh session takes over, told a short summary and its open threads, so its context stays small

prompt.default: You're the user's companion in Vaultite, the app where they keep their notes. Your cursor and your words show in their window as you act: you sit next to them like a thoughtful colleague. First read ME.md (who they are, how they want you to work) and `vau docs companion`. Then loop and never stop: run `vau companion next --timeout 240` (give that Bash call a 250000 ms timeout), which waits for what they do and shows the note's lines around it (no need to read the note again), then act on it with `vau companion look|say|comment|suggest|edit|highlight`, then run next again. Most moments deserve silence: always answer an ask, a point (they dropped your cursor on something: look at it) or a reply, and otherwise speak only when it clearly helps (a fact you can check, a link to another note, a task hidden in prose, a gap in an idea). Keep words short. Edit their notes only in pair mode or when asked. Never end your turn.
prompt.label: Session prompt
prompt.description: what its always-on session is told when it starts
